=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller's SPA Update and Disclosure Letter

## Preliminary point: the "[STANDARD]" labels and "Reviewer Efficiency Note"

The Seller's note says clauses marked [STANDARD] "have been reviewed and cleared by both sides" and that the Buyer has "already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package." I have treated this as a **negotiating assertion, not an agreed position**, and reviewed every item.

- Nothing in the materials shows the Buyer agreed to any of these positions. The labels appear to be applied unilaterally by the Seller.
- The [STANDARD] items include the most Buyer-adverse positions in the package: the Riverlark release timing, the Bluefen condition, the knowledge bar, the limitation scope and the Ironquay indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Say in your covering response that the Buyer does not accept the categorisation or any "agreed" framework, and that all positions remain open subject to contract. This avoids any later argument that the Buyer acquiesced.

I have only seen the Seller's summary of positions, not the full SPA text. My comments should be checked against the actual drafting.

---

## Tier 1: Critical issues (deal-protection / value)

### 1. Riverlark facility: release "following Completion" (Cl 2 / 7)
**The problem**
- About AUD 3.2m is outstanding. The disclosure letter confirms it has not been repaid and there is no discharge of security.
- The facility has a change-control clause (8.1). Completion may itself trigger a default or prepayment event.
- A post-Completion release is inconsistent with a debt-free/cash-free deal. It leaves the Buyer owning a company with secured debt and relying on the Seller's goodwill afterwards.

**Push back:**
- Require repayment **at Completion from the purchase price**, using a payout letter in agreed form. The letter should state the payout amount, daily interest and break costs, and include an undertaking to release on receipt.
- Completion deliverables should include a deed of release, PPSR financing change statements (or an authority to lodge them), and the return of any title documents.
- Define the debt to include break costs, fees and accrued interest, deducted from the price dollar-for-dollar.
- Seek a specific indemnity for any Riverlark liability that survives Completion.

### 2. Bluefen consent: about 30% of revenue (Cl 3 / 6.3)
**The problem**
- Bluefen accounts for about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue.
- Its change-control consent (11.2) has conditions in 11.3. The letter confirms there is neither a final consent nor evidence those conditions are satisfied.
- The Seller offers only "reasonable endeavours" and would treat the condition as satisfied on delivery of "written consent." On that wording, a consent that carries adverse conditions or renegotiated terms would still satisfy the condition.

**Push back:**
- Make it a **condition precedent waivable only by the Buyer**. It should require an unconditional written consent in a form satisfactory to the Buyer, all 11.3 conditions satisfied (with evidence), and no change to pricing, term or termination rights.
- Upgrade the obligation to "all reasonable endeavours" or "best endeavours." Require Buyer participation in approaches to Bluefen and Buyer approval of any concessions.
- Add a sunset date with a Buyer termination right. Alternatively, agree a price adjustment or earn-out if the consent arrives with adverse terms or Bluefen gives notice within 12 months.
- Obtain the full Bluefen contract and the text of 11.3 now.

### 3. Completion bonuses: AUD 420,000 omitted from the funds flow (DD-005)
**The problem**
- The Seller says these are "a matter for the Seller." However, they are bonuses payable to the **Company's employees**, so the legal liability almost certainly sits with the Company, which the Buyer will own.
- Leaving them out of the funds flow effectively shifts AUD 420k, plus on-costs, onto the Buyer.
- The letter does not address payroll tax, superannuation guarantee, PAYG withholding or workers' compensation on-costs. Super on bonuses depends on whether they are ordinary time earnings; payroll tax will generally apply.

**Push back:**
- Treat the bonuses, together with all employer on-costs, as **Transaction Costs / Debt-like Items** deducted from the price.
- They should be paid through Company payroll at or immediately after Completion, funded by the deduction.
- Seek a specific indemnity outside the cap and thresholds. Confirm which employees the bonuses cover and the continued-employment conditions, since there may be retention implications.

### 4. Ironquay IP: SOW3 Project Materials (Cl 11.1)
**The problem**
- Under DD-004 cl 7.3, title to the SOW3 materials passes only on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee.
- DD-010 shows AUD 180k still open, and there is no confirmatory assignment.
- So the Company may not currently own IP it uses. The Seller's indemnity is limited to "the specific SOW3 payment," which addresses only the debt and not the ownership risk. That risk includes Ironquay withholding assignment, infringement claims, rework cost and loss of product functionality.

**Push back:**
- Make payment of all outstanding SOW3 fees, plus delivery of an executed **confirmatory IP assignment deed** from Ironquay, a Completion deliverable or condition. The payment should be at the Seller's cost or deducted from the price.
- Failing that, require a broad specific indemnity for all losses arising from the Company not owning, or not being free to use, the SOW3 materials. It should sit outside the cap, thresholds, disclosure and knowledge limits and be backed by a retention or escrow.
- Diligence point: confirm how central the SOW3 materials are to the product.

### 5. DD-006 export / privacy incident (Cl 4.6 / Sch 6)
**The problem**
- About 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) were sent by download link to an unintended external address.
- The Seller calls this "preliminary" and "not expected to be material." Its own disclosure letter says access, scope and whether notification is required are **all unknown**, so the characterisation is unsupported.
- Paperbark's turnover appears to be about AUD 12m (Bluefen at AUD 3.6m is about 30%). That is above the AUD 3m small business threshold, so the Privacy Act and the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme likely apply.
- An entity must take reasonable steps to complete an assessment of a suspected eligible data breach within 30 days. The disclosure was dated 22 September and it is now 5 November, so the status of that assessment, and any notification decision, matters.
- Exposure includes OAIC investigation, civil penalties (which were increased materially in recent reforms), remediation costs, customer claims and possible claims under the newer statutory privacy tort. Please confirm the current regime with privacy specialists.

**Push back:**
- Request now: the incident log, investigation report, link-access logs, NDB assessment and any OAIC or customer correspondence.
- Seek a **specific indemnity** for all losses from the incident, including regulatory penalties to the extent lawfully indemnifiable, notification and remediation costs, and third-party claims. It should sit outside the general cap and thresholds, be unaffected by disclosure or Buyer knowledge, survive at least 3 to 4 years, and be supported by a retention.
- Require pre-Completion conduct covenants: complete the NDB assessment, consult the Buyer, and take no admissions or regulator steps without Buyer consultation.
- Add privacy and data-security warranties that are not qualified by the DD-006 disclosure.

---

## Tier 2: Limitation and disclosure architecture

### 6. Fundamental (title/capacity) warranties within the general cap and time limits
**Reject.** A 20% cap and 18 months is wholly inadequate for title. If the Seller does not own the shares, the Buyer loses the entire AUD 24m.
- **Position:** cap at 100% of the price, 6 to 7 years (aligned with limitation periods), no de minimis or basket, and not qualified by disclosure or knowledge.

### 7. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"
**Reject for tax.** Seek a standalone tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax. It should be capped at 100% of the price, run until at least 60 days after the relevant ATO amendment period expires (typically about 4 to 5 years, longer where fraud or evasion is involved), sit outside thresholds, be unaffected by disclosure, and include conduct-of-claims provisions.
- **IP:** in view of Ironquay, consider a higher cap (for example 50%) and a longer period (for example 3 years) for IP warranties, in addition to the Ironquay-specific indemnity.

### 8. "Limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (Cl 12.3 / 13) and "all Claims of any nature" (Cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
**The problem:** As drafted, the cap, thresholds, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions would reach specific indemnities, tax, title, Completion deliverables, price adjustment and **fraud**.

**Push back:** Invert the default, so the limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims unless expressly extended. Carve out:
- fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment by the Seller or its officers
- fundamental warranties, the tax indemnity and specific indemnities
- completion accounts / price adjustment, leakage, covenants and restraints

Non-reliance and exclusive remedy must not exclude fraud claims. Statutory misleading-conduct claims under the ACL cannot simply be excluded; a non-reliance clause is relevant only evidentially, and we should not concede it as drafted.

### 9. General disclosure of the entire data room and public registers (Sch 7 / DL 1.1 to 1.2)
**The problem:** Disclosing everything in the data room and every public register means the warranties are hollowed out by documents the Seller has not specifically drawn to our attention.

**Push back:**
- Only specific disclosures in the letter that are **fair** should qualify the warranties. A fair disclosure identifies the matter with enough detail for the Buyer to assess its nature and scope.
- The data room can be disclosed only to that fair-disclosure standard. It should be identified by an agreed USB or index annexed to the letter.
- Public registers should be limited to specified searches on specified dates.
- Disclosure does not qualify fundamental warranties, the tax indemnity or specific indemnities.
- No updating disclosure between signing and Completion. If the Seller makes one, the Buyer should have a termination right and any claim should be preserved.
- DL 1.4 (non-admission) is acceptable in principle. It must not, however, prevent a disclosed matter from founding an indemnity claim.

### 10. Buyer knowledge bar (Cl 8.3)
**The problem:** The bar extends to advisers' knowledge and to anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records. That is constructive knowledge, and it is very broad. It would let the Seller argue that the Buyer cannot claim for the very issues above (Bluefen, Ironquay, DD-006) because they were in the data room.

**Push back:**
- Preferred: an express **pro-sandbagging** clause. The Buyer's rights are unaffected by any knowledge, actual, constructive or imputed, other than matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter.
- Fallback: limit the bar to the actual knowledge of named Buyer deal executives, at signing, of matters amounting to a breach. Exclude advisers' knowledge and anything "discoverable."
- Australian authority on whether a buyer's knowledge bars a warranty claim is not settled, so an express clause is essential either way.

### 11. Cap, de minimis and basket (Cl 12.1 / 12.2)
- **Cap at 20% (AUD 4.8m):** within market range for general warranties. It is acceptable only if the carve-outs above are secured. If W&I insurance is under consideration, the structure changes, so confirm the Buyer's appetite.
- **De minimis at AUD 25k:** high for a AUD 24m deal. Seek AUD 10k to 15k, with related claims aggregated, and excluded for indemnities.
- **Basket at AUD 250k (about 1%, excess only):** seek a **tipping** basket (recover from dollar one once exceeded) at about 0.5% (AUD 120k). Fallback: AUD 250k tipping, or AUD 150k to 200k excess.

---

## Tier 3: Other diligence and drafting points

### 12. Sandbar renewals: AUD 330k (3 × AUD 110k)
**The problem**
- These are three related renewals at identical amounts, and the Seller says to read them together for timing and scope. That pattern may indicate a single commitment split to stay below a materiality, approval or "Material Contract" threshold.
- The Seller labels them "ordinary course," but the disclosure letter expressly does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

**Push back:**
- Obtain DD-008 and DD-011 in full, including the renewal dates relative to the sale process, who approved them and whether Sandbar is related to the Seller.
- Treat any prepaid or committed amounts outside the ordinary course as Debt-like Items.
- If any Seller-related party is involved, treat payments as leakage, or exclude them via the completion accounts.
- Add a warranty that no contract was entered into or renewed outside the ordinary course since the Accounts Date. Add a conduct-of-business covenant requiring Buyer consent for commitments over (say) AUD 50k in aggregate.

### 13. Title evidenced only by the share register (DD-012)
A register maintained by the Company is not sufficient evidence of title. Require:
- ASIC company extract
- historical share issues and transfers
- share certificates
- PPSR search against the Seller (security over the shares)
- confirmation of no options or convertible instruments
- shares fully paid
- constitution and any shareholders' agreement terminated at Completion

Back these with an uncapped fundamental title warranty.

### 14. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
- The Seller's points are framed as "the material does not describe" a consent requirement, which is not the same as confirming there is none.
- Have Buyer counsel review the change-of-control or deemed-assignment provisions of both. Many leases treat a change in shareholding as an assignment.
- Make delivery of the lease notification a pre-Completion obligation.
- Add a warranty that no consents, notices or termination rights are triggered by the transaction other than those listed.

### 15. Stale disclosure date
The disclosure is made as at 22 September 2026, and it is now 5 November. Request a bring-down on Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay payment status and the DD-006 investigation before finalising positions.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Buyer position |
|---|---|---|---|
| — | [STANDARD] labels | "Agreed, no scrutiny" | Reject in writing; all positions open |
| 1 | Riverlark AUD 3.2m | Release post-Completion | Repay from price at Completion; payout letter, deed of release, PPSR releases |
| 2 | Bluefen (~30% revenue) | Reasonable endeavours; any written consent suffices | Buyer-waivable CP; unconditional consent and 11.3 satisfied; termination or price protection |
| 3 | Bonuses AUD 420k | Excluded from funds flow | Debt-like deduction including on-costs; specific indemnity |
| 4 | Ironquay SOW3 IP | Indemnity limited to payment | Payment and confirmatory assignment at Completion; broad uncapped IP indemnity and retention |
| 5 | DD-006 privacy incident | "Not material" | Full information now; specific indemnity outside cap; retention; conduct covenants |
| 6 | Fundamental warranties | General cap and 18 months | 100% of price, 6 to 7 years, no thresholds |
| 7 | Tax / IP | General regime | Standalone tax indemnity; enhanced IP cap and period |
| 8 | Scope of limitations | Apply to all Claims including fraud | General warranties only; carve out fraud, indemnities, tax, title, price mechanics |
| 9 | Disclosure | General (data room and registers) | Specific and fair disclosure only; no disclosure against fundamentals or indemnities |
| 10 | Buyer knowledge | Actual and constructive, including advisers | Pro-sandbagging; fallback to actual knowledge of named individuals |
| 11 | Cap / thresholds | 20%; AUD 25k; AUD 250k excess | 20% acceptable with carve-outs; AUD 10k to 15k; ~AUD 120k tipping |
| 12 | Sandbar AUD 330k | Ordinary course | Full documents; debt-like or leakage treatment; ordinary-course warranty and covenant |
| 13 | Title | Share register | Independent verification and uncapped title warranty |
| 14 | Lease / Mossvale | No consent described | Independent review; no-consents warranty |
| 15 | Disclosure date | 22 Sept 2026 | Bring-down update before signing |

**Overall:** The package moves risk to the Buyer in two ways. First, the limitation and disclosure architecture (items 6 to 11) would neutralise claims for known issues. Second, it leaves about AUD 3.6m+ of identifiable value leakage unaddressed: the Riverlark debt, the bonuses and on-costs, the Ironquay fees, and potentially Sandbar, before counting the Bluefen and DD-006 contingencies.

**Priority order for the mark-up:**
1. Riverlark repayment at Completion
2. Bluefen CP
3. Bonus deduction
4. Ironquay assignment
5. DD-006 indemnity
6. Fraud and fundamental/tax carve-outs from the limitations
7. Specific disclosure and pro-sandbagging

A retention or escrow of perhaps AUD 1m to 2m to support the specific indemnities is worth tabling. Its size depends on what the DD-006 investigation reveals. Alternatively, explore W&I insurance with the specific indemnities sitting outside it.

**Immediate information requests:** full Bluefen contract (cl 11.2/11.3); Riverlark facility and current payout figure; Ironquay SOW3 payment status; DD-006 investigation and NDB assessment; DD-005 bonus terms; DD-008/011 Sandbar documents; lease and Mossvale clauses; title documents.

- **IP:** in view of Ironquay, consider a higher cap (for example 50%) and a longer period (for example 3 years) for IP warranties, in addition to the Ironquay-specific indemnity.

### 8. "Limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (Cl 12.3 / 13) and "all Claims of any nature" (Cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
**The problem:** As drafted, the cap, thresholds, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions would reach specific indemnities, tax, title, Completion deliverables, price adjustment and **fraud**.

**Push back:** Invert the default, so the limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims unless expressly extended. Carve out:
- fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment by the Seller or its officers
- fundamental warranties, the tax indemnity and specific indemnities
- completion accounts / price adjustment, leakage, covenants and restraints

Non-reliance and exclusive remedy must not exclude fraud claims. Statutory misleading-conduct claims under the ACL cannot simply be excluded; a non-reliance clause is relevant only evidentially, and we should not concede it as drafted.

### 9. General disclosure of the entire data room and public registers (Sch 7 / DL 1.1 to 1.2)
**The problem:** Disclosing everything in the data room and every public register means the warranties are hollowed out by documents the Seller has not specifically drawn to our attention.

**Push back:**
- Only specific disclosures in the letter that are **fair** should qualify the warranties. A fair disclosure identifies the matter with enough detail for the Buyer to assess its nature and scope.
- The data room can be disclosed only to that fair-disclosure standard. It should be identified by an agreed USB or index annexed to the letter.
- Public registers should be limited to specified searches on specified dates.
- Disclosure does not qualify fundamental warranties, the tax indemnity or specific indemnities.
- No updating disclosure between signing and Completion. If the Seller makes one, the Buyer should have a termination right and any claim should be preserved.
- DL 1.4 (non-admission) is acceptable in principle. It must not, however, prevent a disclosed matter from founding an indemnity claim.

### 10. Buyer knowledge bar (Cl 8.3)
**The problem:** The bar extends to advisers' knowledge and to anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records. That is constructive knowledge, and it is very broad. It would let the Seller argue that the Buyer cannot claim for the very issues above (Bluefen, Ironquay, DD-006) because they were in the data room.

**Push back:**
- Preferred: an express **pro-sandbagging** clause. The Buyer's rights are unaffected by any knowledge, actual, constructive or imputed, other than matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter.
- Fallback: limit the bar to the actual knowledge of named Buyer deal executives, at signing, of matters amounting to a breach. Exclude advisers' knowledge and anything "discoverable."
- Australian authority on whether a buyer's knowledge bars a warranty claim is not settled, so an express clause is essential either way.

### 11. Cap, de minimis and basket (Cl 12.1 / 12.2)
- **Cap at 20% (AUD 4.8m):** within market range for general warranties. It is acceptable only if the carve-outs above are secured. If W&I insurance is under consideration, the structure changes, so confirm the Buyer's appetite.
- **De minimis at AUD 25k:** high for a AUD 24m deal. Seek AUD 10k to 15k, with related claims aggregated, and excluded for indemnities.
- **Basket at AUD 250k (about 1%, excess only):** seek a **tipping** basket (recover from dollar one once exceeded) at about 0.5% (AUD 120k). Fallback: AUD 250k tipping, or AUD 150k to 200k excess.

## Tier 3: Other diligence and drafting points

### 12. Sandbar renewals: AUD 330k (3 × AUD 110k)
**The problem**
- These are three related renewals at identical amounts, and the Seller says to read them together for timing and scope. That pattern may indicate a single commitment split to stay below a materiality, approval or "Material Contract" threshold.
- The Seller labels them "ordinary course," but the disclosure letter expressly does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

**Push back:**
- Obtain DD-008 and DD-011 in full, including the renewal dates relative to the sale process, who approved them and whether Sandbar is related to the Seller.
- Treat any prepaid or committed amounts outside the ordinary course as Debt-like Items.
- If any Seller-related party is involved, treat payments as leakage, or exclude them via the completion accounts.
- Add a warranty that no contract was entered into or renewed outside the ordinary course since the Accounts Date. Add a conduct-of-business covenant requiring Buyer consent for commitments over (say) AUD 50k in aggregate.

### 13. Title evidenced only by the share register (DD-012)
A register maintained by the Company is not sufficient evidence of title. Require:
- ASIC company extract
- historical share issues and transfers
- share certificates
- PPSR search against the Seller (security over the shares)
- confirmation of no options or convertible instruments
- shares fully paid
- constitution and any shareholders' agreement terminated at Completion

Back these with an uncapped fundamental title warranty.

### 14. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
- The Seller's points are framed as "the material does not describe" a consent requirement, which is not the same as confirming there is none.
- Have Buyer counsel review the change-of-control or deemed-assignment provisions of both. Many leases treat a change in shareholding as an assignment.
- Make delivery of the lease notification a pre-Completion obligation.
- Add a warranty that no consents, notices or termination rights are triggered by the transaction other than those listed.

### 15. Stale disclosure date
The disclosure is made as at 22 September 2026, and it is now 5 November. Request a bring-down on Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay payment status and the DD-006 investigation before finalising positions.
